## Abstract

Entropy is often spoken of as if it did things: as if it drove the arrow of time, pulled the universe toward its end, even pushed and pulled like a force. We argue that this mistakes a measure for a process. Entropy is the name for a result, the amount by which energy has been spread out. It does nothing. The work is done by two things in partnership: **motion**, which shuffles, and **friction**, in its several forms, which scatters ordered motion into disordered motion. Entropy is the score; motion and friction are the players.

The reading is not a rejection of the second law. The bookkeeping is sound, and the score never goes down. What changes is where the agency sits. We show that every increase of entropy has motion behind it, that the motion is driven by a gradient and scattered by friction, even where friction seems absent, and that where motion stops, entropy stops changing. We then follow what is lost when the score is mistaken for a player, from popular accounts of time’s arrow to our own earlier paper The Exhaust Stroke, which we restate.

## 1. Introduction

> Entropy is a name for the results. Friction, in several forms, is the process, and it is paired with motion.

In 1928 Arthur Eddington wrote that the law of increasing entropy “holds, I think, the supreme position among the laws of Nature.” Few physicists would disagree, and we do not. As a law of accounting, the second law of thermodynamics has never been seen to fail.

But somewhere between the textbook and the popular account, the accounting became an actor. Entropy is said to “drive” things: to give time its direction, to doom the universe to a cold end, to explain why eggs break and do not unbreak. In some recent theories it is even proposed as the source of a force. The word has drifted from describing what happened to explaining why.

Our thesis is that **entropy is a measure, not a process.** It is the name for a result: how far energy has been spread out. The processes that do the spreading are motion and friction, working as a pair. Motion shuffles; friction, in its several forms, turns the ordered motion of a whole into the disordered motion of its parts. Entropy records what they have done.

Section 2 sets out what entropy is. Sections 3 and 4 name the players, friction and motion. Section 5 shows that they form a pair, and section 6 finds the tipping point between gathering and scattering. Section 7 follows the cost of mistaking the score for the player, and section 8 applies the correction to our own work.

## 2. What entropy is

> We can be certain of what we invent, never of what we observe.

Entropy was invented, and its inventors were clear about what kind of thing it was.

**Clausius named a quantity.** In 1865 Rudolf Clausius, studying steam engines, needed a way to keep track of how much of an engine’s heat could no longer do work. He defined a quantity, built from the heat exchanged divided by the temperature at which it was exchanged, and named it entropy, from the Greek for transformation. It was a column in a ledger: a way of recording that something irreversible had happened.

**Boltzmann made it a count.** In the 1870s Ludwig Boltzmann showed what the column was counting. Any large collection of particles can be arranged in an enormous number of ways that look the same from outside. Entropy, in his formula, is a measure of how many such arrangements there are. A spread-out state has vastly more arrangements than a bunched-up one, so it has more entropy.

Both definitions describe a state. Neither describes a cause. A ledger does not spend money and a count does not move anything. Entropy tells us how spread out energy is and, compared over time, how much spreading has happened. It does not tell us what did the spreading. For that we have to look at the players.

## 3. What does the work: friction in its forms

> The observations are real. The story isn’t.

The discovery that heat is motion was a discovery about friction.

In 1798 Benjamin Thompson, Count Rumford, was supervising the boring of cannon at the arsenal in Munich. He noticed that a blunt borer grinding against brass produced heat without limit; in one trial it brought a tub of water to the boil in about two and a half hours. If heat were a fluid stored in the metal, as was then believed, it should have run out. It did not. Rumford concluded that the heat came from the motion itself. In the 1840s James Joule made the point exact: a paddle wheel churning water, driven by falling weights, warmed the water by an amount that matched the work done, every time.

Friction, then, is the conversion of ordered motion, the motion of a whole moving together, into disordered motion, the jiggling of its parts. We use the word in that broad sense, and it takes several forms.

- **Sliding friction:** brakes, bearings, a sled on snow, Rumford’s borer.
- **Fluid friction, or viscosity:** Joule’s paddle wheel, air drag, honey resisting the spoon.
- **Electrical friction, or resistance:** a current warming the wire it runs through.
- **Collisional friction:** fast molecules jostling slow ones, so that a hot cup and a cool room drift toward the same temperature.
- **Tidal friction:** the oceans dragged across the sea floor by the Moon, slowing the Earth’s spin so that the day lengthens by a couple of thousandths of a second each century, while the Moon drifts about four centimeters a year farther away.

Every one of these does the same job. It takes motion that could do work and scatters it into motion that mostly cannot. That scattering is what entropy measures.

## 4. The gradient and the leading edge

> Things break and stuff happens.

One case looks at first as if it had no friction at all, and it deserves a close look.

Open a valve between a box of gas and an empty box of the same size. The gas spreads to fill both, and entropy rises. For an ideal gas, the temperature at the end is the same as at the start. It is often described as spreading without friction.

Watch it happen and the description fails. The gas does not seep across molecule by molecule. It rushes. The difference in pressure between the full box and the empty one drives an ordered surge, a real flow with a leading edge. Then the surge breaks up: it strikes the far wall, tumbles back on itself and swirls, and collisions within the gas turn the orderly rush into random motion. That is friction, the fluid kind, working at the leading edge and through the body of the flow. When it is over, the ordered rush has been scattered back into heat, which is why the temperature ends where it began.

The same holds where no surge can be seen. A drop of ink spreads through still water because the difference in concentration works like a difference in pressure, and the spreading is done by molecules jostling their neighbors, which is friction at the smallest scale.

The sky shows the leading edge at full size. When a star explodes, its blast wave sweeps up the gas around it and heats it at the shock front. A shock is friction concentrated at a moving edge.

So the rule needs no exceptions: **every increase of entropy is motion, driven by a gradient and scattered by friction.** The odds that Boltzmann counted remain, as the reason gradients always run downhill and never climb back. They are the bookkeeping of the process, not a separate player in it.

The converse holds too. In 1906 Walther Nernst found that as matter is cooled toward absolute zero, the changes in its entropy shrink toward nothing. As the motion dies away, so does the spreading. Where there is no motion, there is no change in the score, because there is no game.

## 5. A pair

> Heads or tails, one coin. Particle or wave, one substance.

In our paper Two we argued that every pair shows two faces of one thing. Motion and friction are such a pair.

Friction without motion is nothing at all; there is nothing to scatter. Motion without friction is an ideal that nature approaches but never quite reaches. The planets come close, circling for billions of years with almost nothing to slow them, and even they pay a small tax to the tides. Wherever there is motion among many parts, there is friction of some form, and wherever there is friction, there was motion first. They are the same process seen from two sides: motion is what moves, friction is what motion costs.

The pair has a second side that is easy to miss. Friction does not only disperse. It also lets things gather. Gas swirling around a star or a galactic accumulator cannot fall in while it keeps its motion; it would circle forever. Only friction within the swirl, turning orderly circling into heat, lets the gas lose its motion and settle inward. Dust becomes planets the same way, by colliding and sticking. Gravity pulls, but without friction nothing would ever arrive. **Friction is the hinge of both strokes:** it scatters energy outward as heat and lets matter fall inward as mass.

## 6. The tipping point

> We know what we sense. We assume what it is.

If friction serves both strokes, what decides which one wins? Physics has measured the tipping point at every scale, under different names.

- **A single body: escape speed.** A stone thrown from the Earth faster than about eleven kilometers per second leaves for good. Slower, and gravity brings it back.
- **A gas cloud: the Jeans mass.** In 1902 James Jeans worked out when a cloud collapses into stars. If it is massive and cold enough, gravity wins. If its gas is moving too fast, which is to say too hot, motion wins and the cloud disperses.
- **A galactic accumulator: the Eddington limit.** Gas falling inward rubs and heats, and the heat leaves as light that pushes back on the gas still falling. Above a certain brightness the push beats the pull, and infall turns into outflow. Here motion makes friction, friction makes heat and light, and the light outpaces gravity.
- **The whole universe: the critical density.** Expansion is motion; gravity pulls back. Above an average of roughly six hydrogen atoms per cubic meter, gravity would eventually win and everything would fall back together. Below it, the expansion runs on. The measured universe sits remarkably close to that line.

Beneath all four is one rule. **The tipping point depends on whether the heat that friction makes stays or leaves.** If the heat escapes, radiated away into the dark, the motion is lost and gravity wins: clouds cool and collapse into stars, gas settles into accumulators. If the heat is trapped and builds, it becomes pressure and light pushing outward, and dispersal wins: a star holds itself up against its own weight, a quasar blows out winds, a dying star blows apart. Friction serves both strokes, and where its heat goes decides which one it serves.

The tipping point is not a fixed number, like a boiling point. It is a local verdict, reached in the neighborhood. A growing planet stops collecting when it has swept its ring of the disk clean, a size astronomers call the isolation mass. A body can collect only within its sphere of influence, the region where its pull beats its neighbors’; the Moon is ours because it sits inside the Earth’s sphere and not the Sun’s. Galaxies stop making stars when their own accumulators flare and blow the gas out, or when the neighborhood takes it: a galaxy falling into a cluster has its gas stripped by the hot gas it plows through, and a galaxy cut off from fresh supply slowly starves. **Matter keeps collecting while three things hold together: the inward pull beats the heat that friction makes, there is material left to collect, and no neighbor’s stronger pull claims it first.** When any one fails, collecting stops. What a part does depends on the whole around it.

## 7. What the misnaming costs

> Prediction does not equal truth. It’s local and non-transferable.

When the score is mistaken for a player, explanations stop one step short. We suggest three places where that has happened.

**Time’s arrow.** It is often said that entropy gives time its direction. On our reading, the direction comes from motion and friction: ordered motion is scattered and does not unscatter, and every process we can watch runs that way. Entropy records the direction; it does not set it. That leaves the real puzzle standing in plain view, the one our paper The Sister Universe took up: why the beginning was so ordered that there was so much scattering still to do.

**The end of everything.** The universe is said to be heading for “heat death” because entropy must win. On our reading, the fuel runs out because every motion pays its tax to friction, on every turn, everywhere. The Awakening said the fuel always runs out. Friction is how.

**Entropy as a force.** In 2010 Erik Verlinde proposed that gravity itself might be an entropic force. Entropic forces are real in their place: a stretched rubber band pulls back mostly because its long molecules, jiggling, are far more likely to be found bunched than straight. But even there the pull comes from moving molecules acting on the odds. Calling it entropic names the score and credits it with the play. We do not judge Verlinde’s proposal on its merits here. We note only that the name, by putting the agency in the measure, hides where the agency actually is.

## 8. The Exhaust Stroke restated

> The fuel always runs out. Only nothing is inexhaustible.

We made the same mistake ourselves. In The Exhaust Stroke we described the universe as an engine with two strokes, gravity gathering and entropy dispersing, and called entropy the exhaust stroke.

Restated with this paper’s correction: the dispersing stroke is motion and friction scattering ordered motion into heat and spreading matter outward. Entropy is the gauge that reads how far the dispersing has gone. And section 5 adds something the earlier paper lacked: friction also serves the gathering stroke, since nothing gravity pulls can settle without first losing its motion to friction.

So the engine has one moving part on both strokes. Gravity pulls and motion carries; friction decides, on every turn, how much is gathered and how much is scattered. The net, as The Exhaust Stroke argued, is dispersal, and the leak is the expansion we observe. What the engine burns, in the end, is motion, and what it pays for burning it is friction.

## 9. Objections and replies

> Always is not a word in science.

**Objection 1: entropy is fundamental elsewhere.** In 1948 Claude Shannon defined an entropy for information, and black-hole physics assigns entropy to horizons.

_Reply._ Shannon’s entropy is a measure too: of how uncertain a message is before it arrives. It describes; it does not act. Horizon entropy depends on horizons, which our paper What Black Hole? does not grant. In every field, entropy counts something. Counting is not doing.

**Objection 2: “friction” is stretched too far.**

_Reply._ We defined it: any interaction that turns ordered motion into disordered motion. That is the sense Rumford and Joule established when they showed that heat is motion, and it covers sliding, viscosity, resistance, collisions and tides alike. Even the case that seems frictionless, a gas spreading into an empty box, turns out on inspection to be a surge driven by a pressure gradient and broken up by friction at its leading edge.

**Objection 3: the second law cannot be stated without entropy.**

_Reply._ Nor do we want it to be. The ledger stays. Physics needs the score, and the score never goes down. We move only the agency: from the measure to the motion and friction it measures.

**Objection 4: this is only words.**

_Reply._ Words decide where people look. A science that says entropy drives time looks at entropy. A science that says motion and friction drive it looks at motion and friction, and at the one question entropy cannot answer, which is why there was so much ordered motion to begin with.

## 10. Conclusion

> Entropy is the score, not the player.

Entropy was invented as a column in a ledger and refined into a count of arrangements. It is a measure of a result, how far energy has been spread, and it does nothing. The doing is done by motion and friction. Motion shuffles; friction, in its several forms, scatters ordered motion into disorder; every spreading is motion driven down a gradient and scattered by friction at its leading edge; and where motion stops, the score stops changing. Motion and friction are a pair, and friction is the hinge of both strokes of the cosmic engine, scattering energy outward and letting matter settle inward.

What seems clearly not right is crediting a measure with causes: saying entropy drives time, dooms the universe or pulls like a force. The better question is not what entropy does. It is what motion and friction are doing, everywhere and on every turn, and how much of each turn goes to gathering and how much to scattering.

## Abstract

Gravity is the best-measured effect in physics and the least explained. Newton described it exactly and declined to say what it was. Einstein described it as the shape of spacetime, which tells us how bodies move and not what moves them. The particle proposed to carry it has never been found. Gravity is a name for an effect with no face.

We start from a single premise: **Reality is material, and its one activity is motion.** In The Singular Field we proposed that gravity is compression in the material medium of space. Here we take compression one step further, into fluid dynamics. A pressure difference in a fluid does not merely press; it makes the fluid flow. Gravity, on this reading, is an **inflow**, a current of the medium toward mass, and every body in it is carried along. The inflow accounts for why everything falls alike, recovers the familiar strength of gravity at every distance, and has respectable company in the history of physics. Where the inflowing medium goes, we answer with the image of a tidal bay: one medium, one process, two directions, flood, slack water and ebb.

The proposal completes the picture begun in Motion and Friction. Gravity and entropy are not two opposing powers. They are names for two directions of one activity: motion carrying inward, and motion scattering outward through friction. Motion is the common denominator.

## 1. Introduction

> Reality is material. Motion is the common denominator.

Our first paper argued that Reality exists and knowledge is authored. The Singular Field argued that the Reality which exists is material: space is a medium, and everything physics calls a particle or a field is a motion of that medium. This paper takes those two claims as its starting point and asks what they say about the oldest unexplained effect in physics.

In Motion and Friction we argued that entropy is the score, not the player: the processes that spread energy out are motion and friction, and entropy measures how far they have gone. Gravity invites the same correction from the other direction. It too is a name standing where a process should be.

Our thesis is that **gravity is the inflow of the material medium toward mass, a current that carries every body with it.** The compression we proposed earlier is its cause; the inflow is its motion. With that, the two strokes of the cosmic engine have one player. Motion carries inward, which we have called gravity, and motion scatters outward through friction, which we have measured as entropy.

Section 2 shows that gravity has no face in standard physics. Section 3 moves from compression to inflow, section 4 sets out what the inflow explains and section 5 calls witnesses. Section 6 follows the inflow through the tide, section 7 draws the engine with one player, and section 8 meets objections. The proposal is ours, and we label it as a proposal.

## 2. An effect with no face

> We can be certain of what we invent, never of what we observe.

**Newton described it and stopped.** In 1687 Newton gave gravity its law: every body draws every other with a force that weakens with the square of the distance. The law was exact enough to find planets. What it was, he would not say. In 1693 he wrote to Richard Bentley that the idea of one body acting on another at a distance, through nothing, was “so great an absurdity” that no one competent in philosophical matters could fall into it. In 1713, closing the second edition of the _Principia_, he wrote that he had not been able to discover the cause of gravity, and added: _hypotheses non fingo_, I frame no hypotheses.

**Einstein gave it a shape.** In 1915 general relativity replaced the force with geometry: mass curves spacetime, and bodies follow the curves. The theory predicts with extraordinary precision, from the bending of starlight to the ticking of clocks on satellites. But a curve is a description of a path. It says how a body moves, not what moves it. In A Bottom Line we called this geometry obscuring reality.

**The carrier was never found.** Quantum physics carries every other force with a particle, and proposes one for gravity, the graviton. None has been detected, and the energies needed to detect a single one lie far beyond any instrument we could build.

Three centuries, three descriptions, no mechanism. Gravity is known to many decimal places and explained not at all. It is a name for an effect with no face.

## 3. From compression to inflow

> Space is the singular field of Reality.

In The Singular Field we proposed that a massive body changes the state of the medium around it, making it denser nearby and thinner farther out, and that a second body feels more push from the open side than from the side facing the first. We called that compression. It gave gravity a face, but a still one: pressure pressing.

Fluid dynamics says a pressure difference does not stay still. Wherever pressure falls off in one direction, the fluid moves that way. Compression in a material medium is therefore not a standing condition but a current. **The medium flows toward mass.**

On this reading a falling body is not pulled. It is carried, the way a leaf is carried by a river, and it feels nothing as it falls because it moves with the current around it. Standing on the ground is the opposite case: the ground holds us still while the current keeps running past, and what we feel as weight is the push of a current we are not allowed to ride. Compression is the cause; **the inflow** is the motion. In plain words, gravity is a current.

## 4. What the inflow explains

> The question comes from the senses. The answer comes from experience, if we live that long.

**Why everything falls alike.** Galileo argued that bodies of different weight fall together, and in 1971 the Apollo 15 astronaut David Scott dropped a hammer and a feather on the Moon and watched them land at the same moment. In 2022 the MICROSCOPE satellite confirmed the rule to about one part in a million billion. General relativity takes the rule as a starting principle and does not explain it. The inflow explains it at once: everything in the current is carried by the same current at the same rate, whatever it weighs. A leaf and a log go down the river together.

**Why gravity weakens as it does.** Suppose the inflow at each distance from a mass runs at the speed a body would need to escape from that distance. Then the current speeds up as it nears the mass, and the rate at which it speeds up falls off with the square of the distance. That rate is exactly the acceleration Newton’s law gives. This is not our invention; it is the mathematics of the river model described in section 5, and it reproduces the predictions of general relativity around a single mass.

**Why the medium is denser near mass.** If the same amount of medium crosses every sphere around a mass as it flows inward, and it speeds up as it goes, it must also crowd together. Worked out, the medium grows denser toward the mass in a definite way. That is the compression of The Singular Field, arrived at from the other side: the denser medium near mass is what a converging current looks like.

**Why light bends.** Light travels through the medium at its own fixed speed. Where the medium is moving, light is carried with it, the way a swimmer crossing a river is carried downstream. Light passing a star is swept slightly toward it, which is the bending first measured in 1919.

## 5. Supporting witnesses

> Intelligence should always be respected, no matter what form it comes in.

The proposal is ours. Others have walked parts of the road.

**Carl Anton Bjerknes**, in the 1870s, showed experimentally that spheres pulsing in water attract or repel one another in ways that mimic gravity and electricity. The forces between them were carried entirely by the motion of the water.

**Paul Painlevé and Allvar Gullstrand**, independently in 1921 and 1922, found a way of writing Einstein’s solution for a single mass in which space itself flows inward at the escape speed. For decades it was treated as a mathematical curiosity.

**William Unruh**, in 1981, showed that sound in a flowing fluid behaves like light near a dense object: where the flow outruns the speed of sound, sound cannot swim back upstream. His “dumb holes” founded the field of analogue gravity, now studied in laboratory fluids.

**Andrew Hamilton and Jason Lisle**, in 2008, made Painlevé and Gullstrand’s mathematics into a picture they called the river model: space flowing inward like a river, with objects and light moving through the river as fish swim through water. They presented it as a way of seeing general relativity, not as a claim about what space is.

Our step is the one they did not take. We read the river as real, a material medium actually flowing, because Reality is material.

## 6. The tide: where the inflow goes

> One process, one medium, two directions.

If the medium flows toward mass without pause, it must go somewhere. The answer we propose comes from a bay.

The tide flows in, slack water comes at the changeover, and the tide flows out. One medium, one process, two directions. The tide does not simply turn back where it came in. It flows until it meets resistance, and then it ebbs on the other side. Within that cycle, matter moves by a rule every river pilot knows.

1. **Motion carries matter to a friction point.** Wherever the flow meets resistance, it slows and drops what it carries.
2. **The friction point accretes.** Each deposit adds resistance, which slows the flow further, which enlarges the next deposit.
3. **It grows until it balances.** The deposit builds until its resistance equals the force of the flow. This is slack water at the scale of a sandbar.
4. **The flow reroutes.** Blocked, the motion alters its pattern toward lower resistance.
5. **And it steals along the way.** The rerouted current scours new ground and carries matter off: the ebb taking what the flood brought.

**On Earth the record is exact.** In 1935 Filip Hjulström charted how the speed of a current decides whether it erodes, carries or drops its load. Rivers build up their own beds until they are blocked, then jump to a new course, which geologists call avulsion. The Mississippi has shifted its delta every thousand years or so, abandoning the old lobe to the sea.

**In the sky the sequence repeats.** Gas flows inward through the broad disk around a galactic accumulator. Friction heats it, and matter piles up at the center. The pile grows until the heat friction makes pushes back as hard as the inflow presses in, the balance astronomers call the Eddington limit. Then the flow reroutes along the path of least resistance: the jets, thrown out along the poles, the one direction where nothing is piled in the way. And the jets steal as they go, dragging surrounding gas along with them, while the winds strip the host galaxy of the gas it would need for new stars.

So the inflow is neither swallowed nor drained. It is stored until balance and then returned, by one process in two directions. Slack water is the tipping point of Motion and Friction: a local verdict, set by the neighborhood. On the largest scale, what if the expansion of the emptiest regions is the ebb, and the gathering around mass the flood, so that the universe is a tidal bay and not a set of drains? That last step has not been worked out, and it is labeled _pending_.

**Slack water now.** If the universe is a tidal bay, the record suggests where in the tide we stand: at slack water, in its middle range. For most of its history the expansion was slowing, the gathering side holding the upper hand; some five or six billion years ago it stopped slowing and began to speed up. The tide has turned, and recently. Galaxies made stars fastest about ten billion years ago, and the rate has fallen ever since; the flood has passed its height. And the two sides stand nearly even today. Cosmologists note that the two great budgets of their model, the gathering matter and whatever drives the expansion, happen to be about the same size in our era, though they were wildly unequal in the past and will be again. They call it the coincidence problem and ask why we should live at the one time of balance. On our reading the answer is that balance is what slack water is. The middle range belongs to the tide, the gathering and its turn. By the clock of the stars, which will burn for trillions of years, the universe is still young.

**A continuing tide.** Reality is a continuing tide as space expands. On the largest scale the expansion is the ebb, and wherever mass gathers the flood goes on, locally, turn after turn. The tide needs no driver outside itself. Flood and ebb are the first pair, matter and motion, working in two directions in one medium.

## 7. One player, two directions

> Heads or tails, one coin. Particle or wave, one substance.

With gravity given a face, the cosmic engine described in The Exhaust Stroke and restated in Motion and Friction has a single player.

- **Motion** is the player: the one activity of a material Reality.
- **The inflow** carries inward. It is the gathering stroke, and gravity is its old name.
- **Friction** scatters outward. It is the dispersing stroke, turning ordered motion into disorder.
- **Entropy** is the score of the scattering.
- **The tipping point** between them is a local verdict, set by the neighborhood: matter keeps collecting while the inflow beats the heat friction makes, while there is material to collect, and while no neighbor’s stronger current claims it first.

In the language of the bay, the gathering stroke is the flood, the dispersing stroke is the ebb, and the tipping point is slack water. The engine and the tide are two pictures of the same thing: one medium, one process, two directions.

In our paper Two we argued that every pair shows two faces of one thing. Gravity and entropy have been taught as two great principles of nature, one pulling things together and one pulling them apart. On this reading they are not two principles. They are two directions of one activity, motion in and motion out, heads and tails of one coin.

## 8. Objections and replies

> Science is strongest where it can touch, and weakest where it can only watch.

**Objection 1: this is the ether, and the ether was refuted.**

_Reply._ The Singular Field met this at length. The experiments of Michelson and Morley could not detect motion through a medium, and they could not have if the instruments themselves are made of the medium. The objection removes a medium that matter moves through. It does not touch a medium that matter is made of.

**Objection 2: a current would drag on the planets.**

_Reply._ Drag is friction between a body and a fluid. A body falling with the current has nothing to rub against. A body in orbit does move across the current, and for the planets to circle for billions of years with no measurable slowing, the medium must flow without friction, as a superfluid does. That is a real requirement on the medium, and we accept it.

**Objection 3: the river model is only a way of picturing general relativity.**

_Reply._ Around a single mass the two give the same predictions, which is a strength: the inflow agrees with every test general relativity has passed there. The difference is in the reading. Hamilton and Lisle offered the river as a picture; we offer it as the thing itself. Where a material medium and a geometry diverge, close to the densest objects and in the waves they send out, The Singular Field lists tests that could tell them apart.

**Objection 4: many masses.** The river picture is exact for one mass. Around two or more, the currents must combine, and general relativity does not simply add them.

_Reply._ Agreed. The mathematical form of the medium, which The Singular Field left _pending_, must also say how currents combine. That is open work.

## 9. Conclusion

> We don’t challenge the vision, we sharpen the focus.

Newton measured gravity and would not say what it was. Einstein drew its shape. The particle meant to carry it has never been seen. For three centuries gravity has been a name for an effect with no face.

We have proposed a face. Reality is material, and its one activity is motion. The compression in the medium that The Singular Field proposed is not a standing pressure but a current: the medium flows toward mass, and every body in it is carried along. The current explains why everything falls alike, matches the strength of gravity at every distance, and agrees with the river model that others drew as a picture and we read as real. It leaves one sharp question open, where the inflowing medium goes, and we have answered it with the tide: stored until balance, then returned, one process in two directions, its largest scale still _pending_.

With that, gravity and entropy are no longer two opposed powers. They are two directions of one activity, motion carrying in and motion scattering out. Motion is the common denominator.

What seems clearly not right is a physics that measures gravity to many decimal places and accepts, for three hundred years, that it has no cause. The better question is not what gravity is made of. It is where the current comes from, and where it goes.

## Abstract

In Two we argued that pairs are primary: nothing in Reality comes single. This paper sets out the theory that the earlier work assumed. We name the first pair, **matter and motion**, and argue that every other pair in nature is an arrangement of these two. Matter is what is there; motion is what it does. Neither has ever been found without the other.

From the first pair follow five principles. Opposites are conjoined, not attracted. They are made together and unmade together. Neither face of a pair is ever found alone. A pair that looks lopsided points to its missing half. And a name that shows only one face of a pair, such as gravity, entropy or attraction, is a name for an effect, not a description of a process. We trace the ladder of pairs from the first pair to the choices made by every living thing, call two witnesses who stood near the idea, and meet the objections. The theory is ours, and it is offered as a way of seeing, with consequences that can be checked.

## 1. Introduction

> Opposites don’t attract. They are conjoined.

The work collected in these papers keeps meeting pairs. Particle and wave. Matter and antimatter. North and south. Gathering and dispersing. Something and nothing. Cosmic and cognitive. To be and not to be. Each time, the pair has turned out to be not two things but one thing with two faces: heads and tails, one coin.

Until now we have met the pairs one at a time. This paper asks what they have in common and where they begin. Our thesis is that **Reality is material, its first pair is matter and motion, and every other pair is that first pair arranged in some way.** From that starting point, five principles follow, each of which can be checked against what is observed.

Section 2 names the first pair. Sections 3 to 7 set out the five principles. Section 8 climbs the ladder of pairs from the first to the most human. Sections 9 to 11 call witnesses, meet the objections and conclude.

## 2. The first pair: matter and motion

> Reality is material. Motion is the common denominator.

Matter is what is there. Motion is what it does. The two have never been found apart.

**No matter without motion.** Cool matter as close to absolute zero as any laboratory can manage, and it still moves. Quantum physics says it must: even in its lowest possible state, a particle keeps a residual jitter that cannot be removed, which physicists call zero-point motion. Helium, held by that jitter, refuses to freeze at ordinary pressure no matter how cold it gets. Matter at rest is a limit approached and never reached.

**No motion without matter.** Motion is always the motion of something. Light is a motion of the medium, sound a motion of air, heat a motion of atoms, and in The Singular Field we argued that space itself is a material medium, so that even what travels through empty space is a motion of something real. A motion with nothing moving has never been observed, and it is not clear what it would mean.

So matter and motion are not two things that happen to occur together. They are two faces of one Reality: what is there, and what it does. That is the first pair. Everything after it is an arrangement of these two faces.

**Energy is constrained motion.** Physics defines energy as a conserved quantity, the capacity to do work, and leaves open what it is. In a material medium the question has an answer. Motion that flows freely is simply motion. Motion that is held back, by resistance, compression or confinement, becomes tension, and energy is that tension and its release. Potential energy is the medium compressed or strained. Mass, by Einstein’s E = mc², is motion confined in one place: nearly all the mass of a proton comes from the motion and binding of what is inside it, not from the masses of its three quarks. And energy shows itself where motion meets resistance, at the friction point described in Motion and Friction, as a release of tension: heat, light, a blow, a shock. Free motion carries energy as unused potential: a body coasting through the medium holds what it will release when it meets resistance. How much it holds depends on what it meets, since a body’s kinetic energy differs from one observer to the next and is fixed only against the thing it strikes. Energy is therefore not a third member beside matter and motion. It is motion under constraint, and the conservation of energy is the ledger of the first pair.

## 3. First principle: conjoined, not attracted

> Heads or tails, one coin. Particle or wave, one substance.

Physics says opposites attract: positive draws negative, north draws south. “Attract” names an effect at a distance and says nothing about how it happens. The theory says something different. **Opposites are not two things drawn together. They are one thing with two faces.**

The difference matters. Two things that attract could, in principle, exist apart and then meet. Two faces of one thing cannot. On this reading, what looks like a pull between opposites is the tendency of the two faces of one disturbance in the medium to be whole again. In Gravity Has No Face we argued that what looks like a pull between masses is a current in the medium. The same move applies here: the pull is a name; the process is the medium’s own motion.

## 4. Second principle: made together, unmade together

> One is what didn’t bang. Two is the first thing that did.

If opposites are faces of one thing, they should come into being together and go out of being together. They do.

In 1933 Patrick Blackett and Giuseppe Occhialini photographed a single burst of high-energy light turning into an electron and a positron at one point: one thing becoming a pair. When an electron and a positron meet, the pair vanishes back into light. Every particle made in every collider arrives with its antiparticle. Electric charge has never been created or destroyed, only separated and rejoined. In 1918 Emmy Noether proved that every symmetry of nature carries a conservation law, so that nothing can be added to one side of the ledger without the other.

In The Singular Field and in Two we described this as a twist in the medium that cannot be made without a counter-twist. The second principle states it generally: **a pair is made in one act and unmade in one act.**

## 5. Third principle: no lone face

> We know what we sense. We assume what it is.

If opposites are faces of one thing, neither face should ever be found alone.

**The magnet.** Cut a magnet and each piece has both poles. In 1931 Paul Dirac showed that a lone magnetic pole would be consistent with quantum theory, and physicists have searched for one ever since, in cosmic rays, in ancient rock and at the Large Hadron Collider. None has been found.

**The quark.** No quark has ever been seen alone. Pull two apart and the effort spent makes a new pair, so that separation yields two conjoined pairs, never one divided one.

**Action and reaction.** In 1687 Newton stated that to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. No push has ever been found without its push back.

The third principle is a prediction as well as a summary: **no lone face of a pair will be found.**

## 6. Fourth principle: the lopsided pair points to its other half

> The observations are real. The story isn’t.

If every pair balances, then a pair that looks lopsided is a clue: its other half is somewhere we have not yet looked.

Physics has followed this clue twice and been rewarded both times. In 1928 Dirac’s equation for the electron produced a second set of solutions that seemed to describe nothing known. He took them seriously, and in 1932 Carl Anderson found the positron, the electron’s opposite, in cosmic rays. In 1930 the energy books of radioactive decay would not balance; Wolfgang Pauli proposed an unseen particle to carry the missing share, and in 1956 Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines detected the neutrino.

The largest lopsided pair is the universe itself. It holds far more matter than antimatter, it runs one way in time, and one of its forces favors one hand. In The Sister Universe we followed the fourth principle to its limit and asked, as a thought exercise, whether those imbalances point to a sister with opposite features. **A lopsided ledger is not an accident. It is a map to the missing column.**

## 7. Fifth principle: names with one face

> Gravity is a name for an effect with no face.

If every process is the first pair at work, then a name that describes only one face of a pair, or only its result, describes an effect and hides a process. Three such names have carried a great deal of physics.

**Gravity** names the gathering face. In Gravity Has No Face we gave it a process: matter compresses the medium, and the medium’s motion carries matter inward. Matter shapes the current; the current carries matter.

This is more than a renaming. If gravity is the inflow of motion into gathered matter, it is not a third entity beside matter and motion, and the account needs no separate force acting across empty space. Gravity is the first pair itself, observed from the side where matter gathers.

**Entropy** names the score of the scattering face. In Motion and Friction we gave it its players: motion driven down a gradient and scattered by friction.

**Attraction** names the effect of a conjoined pair seen from outside, as section 3 argued.

In our first paper we called such words placeholders when they stand where knowledge should be. The fifth principle explains why placeholders arise: **a name that shows one face of a pair has lost sight of the other.** Restoring the missing face turns the name back into a process.

## 8. The ladder of pairs

> To be or not to be: the principal duality, inherent in every decision.

If every pair is the first pair arranged, the pairs should form a ladder, each rung built from the one below. They do.

1. **Matter and motion.** The first pair: what is there, and what it does.
2. **Gathering and scattering.** Motion acting on matter in two directions: the inflow carrying it in, friction scattering it out. In the language of the bay, flood and ebb.
3. **Particle and wave.** The medium moving is the wave; the medium meeting resistance is the particle, as The Singular Field argued.
4. **Twist and counter-twist.** Matter and antimatter, positive and negative, north and south: the faces of one disturbance in the medium.
5. **Something and nothing.** The bounds of the first pair. The fuel always runs out; only nothing is inexhaustible.
6. **Mind and meaning.** What is there, and what it does, on the cognitive face. As Two Faces of Reality argued, mind is matter arranged to know; what mind does is make meaning.
7. **Insignificance and uniqueness.** The two faces of the knower, as The Awakening argued.
8. **To be and not to be.** The principal duality, the choice between caution and curiosity that lies inside every decision of every living thing, as This or Nothing argued.

The ladder runs from the first pair to the last choice, and every rung is one coin with two faces. The work in these papers did not set out to build it. It found the rungs one at a time and only now sees that they stand on one another.

Two of the rungs mirror each other. Matter and motion are what is there and what it does on the cosmic face of Reality; mind and meaning are what is there and what it does on the cognitive face. The old phrase “mind and matter” names two stuffs and looks for a joint between them. The theory finds instead one Reality with two faces, each with its own first pair, and mind, as matter arranged to know, built from the first.

## 9. Supporting witnesses

> Intelligence should always be respected, no matter what form it comes in.

The theory is ours. Two witnesses stood near it, twenty-five centuries apart.

**Heraclitus**, around 500 BC, wrote that “the road up and the road down are one and the same,” and that people do not understand how a thing at variance with itself agrees with itself, like the opposing tension of the bow and the lyre. He saw opposites as one process seen from two sides.

**Niels Bohr**, in 1927, proposed that light and matter show two faces, wave and particle, that cannot be seen at once but are both needed for a complete account. He called it complementarity. When Denmark gave him its highest honor in 1947, he chose for his coat of arms the yin-yang symbol and the motto _Contraria sunt complementa_: opposites are complementary.

What neither did was name the first pair, or trace the ladder from it to everything else.

## 10. Objections and replies

> Always is not a word in science.

**Objection 1: not every opposite is a pair in nature.** Hot and cold, up and down, left and right are human labels.

_Reply._ Many are, and they live on the cognitive face, where we sort the world. The theory concerns pairs that nature makes in one act and unmakes in one act. Even so, many human labels mark something real underneath: hot and cold mark a difference in motion, which is the first pair at work.

**Objection 2: this is a way of talking, not a theory.**

_Reply._ Two of its principles stand on the record. The third says no lone face will be found, and none has been. The fourth says a lopsided ledger points to a missing half: it is the reasoning that found the positron and the neutrino, and it is the reasoning behind The Sister Universe.

**Objection 3: nature also makes threes.** Quarks come in three colors, and protons are made of three quarks.

_Reply._ Each color has its anticolor, and the three combine into a whole that carries no color at all. The bookkeeping is still paired: every charge with its opposite, every color with its anticolor.

**Objection 4: matter at absolute zero would not move.**

_Reply._ Absolute zero cannot be reached; Nernst’s work on the third law of thermodynamics showed it can only be approached. And quantum physics says matter keeps a residual motion even in its lowest state. Matter without motion is a limit, never a thing.

## 11. Conclusion

> We don’t challenge the vision, we sharpen the focus.

Reality is material, and its first pair is matter and motion: what is there, and what it does. Neither has been found without the other. From that pair five principles follow. Opposites are conjoined, not attracted. They are made together and unmade together. Neither face is ever found alone. A lopsided pair points to its missing half. And a name that shows one face of a pair names an effect and hides a process.

The pairs form a ladder, from matter and motion to gathering and scattering, from twist and counter-twist to something and nothing, from mind and meaning to the choice between this and nothing that every living thing makes every day. Every rung is one coin with two faces.

Taken together, the principles amount to one prediction about Reality as a whole: that it is binary. It keeps its accounts by double entry, each entry matched by its counter-entry, and the whole of matter balanced against the whole of motion. A single-entry Reality, a face without its pair, has not been found, and the theory holds that it will not be.

What seems clearly not right is treating the pairs of nature as coincidences, or the forces between opposites as pulls across empty space. The better question is not why opposites attract. It is what single thing each pair is a face of, and where its other face has gone.
