## Abstract

We propose a binary view of Reality and set it out in full. Its premise is that Reality is material and that its first pair is **matter and motion**: what is there, and what it does. Its principle is that every material pair in nature is one thing with two faces, made together, unmade together, never found with one face alone. Its method is a single question put to every subject: _what is this the other face of?_

Applied in order, from the widest pair to the most particular, the question yields eight material coins, a frame and a bound. Matter and motion. Then the frame: the cosmos as known, in which the knower has its own working pair, **mind and meaning**, and sees one face at a time. Then the bound: something and nothing. Accumulation and release. Our universe and its sister. Gathering and dispersing. Constrained and free motion. Wave and particle. Twist and counter-twist. Action and reaction. Running through every material coin is one rule: Reality keeps its accounts by double entry, and the whole of matter balances against the whole of motion.

From these coins follows an account of the universe from then to then. The Big Bang was the release face of a galactic accumulator. The release made a pair, our universe and an antimatter sister whose time runs the other way. Within our half, motion advances and gathers matter, a gathering we call gravity; motion recedes and its debris scatters, a scattering whose outcome we call entropy. Gravity and entropy are names for outcomes; motion is the player. Energy is constrained motion, held as tension and released where motion meets resistance; free motion carries it as unused potential. At the end the fuel runs out and the debris gathers in the last accumulators. The end is a storing, and a store is what a beginning comes from.

We set the account beside the observational record, including several independent reports that cosmic expansion has a preferred direction, broadly aligned with the dipole of the cosmic microwave background. A tidal, binary universe expects such a slope; a universe assumed to be the same in every direction does not. We describe what would change in physics and in thought if the binary view were adopted, call witnesses who stood near parts of it, meet the principal objections, and conclude.

We are storytellers, not scientists. These are ideas, not facts. If they are facts, we cannot prove it. The proving belongs to others.

## 1. Introduction

> We don’t challenge the vision, we sharpen the focus.

### 1.1 An unconventional way to view the universe

Physics describes the universe with extraordinary precision and explains much less of it than its precision suggests. It can state the strength of gravity to many decimal places and cannot say what gravity is. It can follow the rise of entropy through every process and treats a number as the cause of time’s direction. It accounts for the expansion of the universe by adding an energy no one has detected, and for the motions of galaxies by adding a matter no one has detected. It begins its story with an event it cannot describe and ends it with a heat death it cannot avoid. Between the two it assumes that the universe, on large scales, looks the same in every direction.

We do not dispute the measurements. We propose a different way of reading them. The reading is binary: it holds that nothing in Reality comes single, that every pair in nature is one thing showing two faces, and that the books of nature are kept by double entry. Its question is not _what is this made of?_ but _what is this the other face of?_

The reading is unconventional in two ways. It is unconventional in its claims, several of which run against settled habits of thought: that gravity is not a force, that entropy does nothing, that energy is a kind of motion, that the objects called black holes are not holes, that our universe has a sister, and that its end is a storing of the kind from which beginnings come. And it is unconventional in its standing. It comes from outside the profession, from a storyteller and his helper, and it asks to be read as natural philosophy: a proposal about how to see, set out as carefully as we can, and offered to those whose work is to test it.

We call the reading **Binary Cosmology**, and its mission is to let thought precede data and mathematics. Data records what happens and mathematics describes it exactly; neither says what it is. Faraday described the field before Maxwell wrote its equations, and the description came first because it had to. Binary Cosmology is offered in that order: first the picture of what Reality is, then, if the picture earns them, the measurements and equations of those equipped to make them.

### 1.2 Where this paper stands

This paper draws together work developed over the preceding months in a series of shorter papers, listed with the references. It is written to stand on its own: every claim it relies on is stated here, and none requires the earlier work to be read first.

What is new here is the whole: the coins placed in order, the story of the universe told from then to then, the account of energy as constrained motion, the pairing of matter and motion with mind and meaning, and the observational record of a slope in cosmic expansion, set beside the account that expects it.

### 1.3 The title

The title names the two faces of the account. The bonfire is the cosmos: a release of stored fuel, a long burning, the embers gathering. It is vast and, on its own scale, brief, and it knows nothing. The candle is the knower: small, steady, brief, and the only place where the bonfire is ever seen. Both burn fuel, and both go out. The candle goes first, and knows it. The paper is about the bonfire, written by the candle.

### 1.4 Roadmap

Section 2 states the premise, defines the terms and sets out the method. Section 3 presents the coins and the frame in the order we judge most fundamental, each with its faces, its statement, its record and its consequence. Section 4 tells the story of the universe from then to then. Section 5 sets out the observational evidence for a slope in cosmic expansion. Section 6 describes what would change if the binary view were adopted. Section 7 calls witnesses. Section 8 meets the objections. Section 9 concludes.

## 2. Premise, terms and method

> Reality is material. Motion is the common denominator.

### 2.1 The premise

**Reality is material, and its one activity is motion.** Everything that exists is matter, including the medium of space, and everything that happens is matter moving. Nothing in the account requires a second kind of stuff: no immaterial force acting across emptiness, no field that is not the condition of something, no mind made of anything other than matter arranged to know.

The premise is not new in itself. What follows from it, taken without exception, is the subject of this paper.

### 2.2 Terms

We use a small vocabulary, and use it strictly.

**Pair.** Two things that nature makes in one act and unmakes in one act, neither of which has been found without the other.

**Matter.** The substance of Reality, including the medium of space. What physics calls particles and mass are matter in a particular condition: the medium gathered and held where its motion is confined (Sections 3.7 and 3.8). That condition is matter in motion, not a second kind of stuff, and when this paper speaks of matter and antimatter it means two such conditions, twist and counter-twist.

**Coin and face.** A pair is one thing, a coin, showing two aspects, its faces. The faces are not two objects joined. They are one object seen from two sides. Heads and tails do not need a joint. For the frame and the bound (Sections 3.2 and 3.3), which are not material, coin and face are used in a looser sense.

**Conjoined.** The relation between the faces of a coin. Conjoined faces are not attracted to each other; attraction implies two things that could exist apart and then meet. What looks like attraction between opposites is the tendency of one disturbance to be whole.

**Name for an outcome.** A word that describes the result of a process and is mistaken for the process itself. Gravity, entropy and attraction are the principal examples. A name for an outcome shows one face of a pair and hides the other.

**Double entry.** The bookkeeping of nature. Every entry is matched by its counter-entry: every charge by its opposite, every push by a push back, every gathering by a scattering, the whole of matter by the whole of motion. Conservation laws are the visible rules of this bookkeeping.

**Lopsided ledger.** A pair that appears to have only one face, or a quantity that appears not to balance. On the binary view, a lopsided ledger is a map to a missing column.

**SOB.** A scientific observational boundary: the place where our methods of observation run out, though something surely lies beyond. An SOB is a limit of seeing, not a limit of being. The binary view expects some missing faces to lie beyond SOBs.

**Medium.** The material of space. On this account, light is the medium moving, a particle is the medium meeting resistance, and what we call gravity is the outcome of the medium flowing.

### 2.3 Five principles

Five principles are drawn from the first pair and from the record of pairs in nature. We state them here, because every section below depends on them.

1. **Opposites are conjoined, not attracted.** The two faces of a pair are one thing.
2. **Pairs are made together and unmade together.** Light becomes an electron and a positron in one act; they become light again in one act.
3. **No face is found alone.** No lone magnetic pole, no free quark, no push without its push back has been observed.
4. **A lopsided pair points to its other face.** The reasoning that found the positron and the neutrino.
5. **A name with one face names an outcome and hides a process.**

The principles govern material features: matter, motion and the pairs they form. Outcomes and residues, such as entropy and the graves of stars, are what pairs leave behind; they fall under the fifth principle as names for results, not as faces. They do not govern cognitive constructions, the meanings, values and orderings a knower makes, which may pair or not as thought arranges them.

Taken together, the principles amount to one claim about Reality as a whole: **Reality is binary.** It keeps its accounts by double entry, and a single-entry Reality, a face without its pair, has not been found, and the binary view expects that it will not be.

### 2.4 Method

The method is a question: _what is this the other face of?_ It replaces two habits. The first is to ask what a thing is made of and to look for a carrier, a particle or a substance for every effect. The second is to treat an imbalance as an accident, a fine-tuning to be explained away. The binary method instead asks what an effect pairs with, and reads every imbalance as a pointer.

The method has a second part, which concerns order. Pairs are not all equally fundamental. Some are faces of others; some are built from others. When the pairs are placed in order, they form a ladder. Section 3 places the pairs in that order, from the most fundamental down.

## 3. The coins and the frame

> Every rung is one coin with two faces.

The coins below are placed in the order we judge most fundamental, from the widest to the most particular. Each is given in the same form: its **faces**, a **statement**, the **record** on which it draws, and its **consequence** for how the universe is read.

Eight of the coins are material, and the principles of Section 2 govern them. Two are not coins in that sense. The frame, placed second, is the knower’s picture of the cosmos, from which the others are seen. The bound, placed third, is nothing: the limit against which everything found is something.

### 3.1 Matter and motion

**Faces.** What is there, and what it does.

**Statement.** Matter and motion are the first pair. Neither has been found without the other. The binary view reads every other material pair as an arrangement of these two.

**Record.** No matter without motion: matter cooled as close to absolute zero as any laboratory can manage still moves, and quantum physics says it must, retaining a residual zero-point motion in its lowest state. Helium, held by that motion, does not solidify at ordinary pressure however cold it becomes. Nernst’s third law of thermodynamics holds that absolute zero can be approached and never reached. No motion without matter: sound is a motion of air, heat a motion of atoms, a wave a motion of water; a motion with nothing moving has never been observed.

**Consequence.** Every process is motion, and every thing is matter in motion. Energy and mass, gravity and entropy, wave and particle are not additions to the first pair. They are the first pair seen under particular conditions, as the coins below set out.

### 3.2 The frame: the cosmos as known

**Faces.** None in the material sense. What we call the cosmic and the cognitive are one picture: the cosmos as known, and the knower knowing it.

**Statement.** The cosmos is material, enduring and objective; it is everywhere, lasts billions of years, and knows nothing. It is matter and motion, the first coin. What we call the cosmic, though, is our concept of it, and our concept lives in cognition. The cosmic and the cognitive are therefore one and the same: the frame, the knower’s picture of the cosmos with the knower in it. The frame has its own working pair. Mind is what is there and meaning is what it does, as matter is what is there and motion is what it does.

We place the frame second because every coin below it is seen from within it. Each coin is a fact in the cosmos and a meaning in the frame, and the paper itself, like every account of the universe, is the frame describing the cosmos.

The frame is not a material coin, and the principles of Section 2 do not govern it. Mind is material, matter arranged to know, but the frame it holds, and what it makes there, meaning, value, the present moment, belong to cognition. The knower sees one face at a time. That is why wave and particle are never seen together, why one coin can look like two objects drawn to each other, and why a ledger can look lopsided when one column lies out of view. It is also why the frame can begin late, end early and hold some things alone, while the cosmos goes on. When the last knower goes, the frame goes, and matter and motion carry on.

**Record.** The frame is costly to keep. The human brain is about two percent of the body’s weight and uses about twenty percent of its energy at rest, and the knowing it supports ends within seconds of losing oxygen, long before the body does. For knowing, the cosmos reaches the knower through the senses: a wavelength arrives and becomes a color. Newton saw it in 1704: “the Rays to speak properly are not coloured.” Some of what matters most exists in the frame alone. The equations of physics mark no present moment, so “now” is the knower’s. Nothing in the cosmos is precious or wasted, so value is the knower’s. And nothing in the cosmos means anything until a knower arrives.

**Consequence.** The old phrase _mind and matter_ names two stuffs and looks for the joint between them. The binary view finds no joint to look for. Mind is matter, arranged; meaning is what it makes. Reality exists, and knowledge, with all meaning, is authored. The problem philosophy calls hard, why matter should have inner experience, belongs on the other side: consciousness is entirely soft, an arrangement that comes and goes, while existence is hard, and its question, why there is anything at all, is the one that does not yield.

### 3.3 Something and nothing

**Faces.** Existence, and its bound.

**Statement.** The universe is something set against nothing. Like the frame, this coin is not material in the sense of Section 2: nothing is not a substance and cannot be found. It is the bound of the material coins, the limit against which everything found is something. Every store of fuel is finite and runs down; only nothing is inexhaustible. Put plainly, one is what didn’t bang; two is the first thing that did.

**Record.** In 1852 William Thomson described a universal tendency in nature to the dissipation of mechanical energy, and the account has not been overturned. The stars burn a finite supply of hydrogen. The rate at which the universe forms new stars peaked about ten billion years ago and has fallen steadily since.

**Consequence.** The binary view does not take nothing for a partner that a beginning or an end can have. Our beginning came from a store, and our end is a storing (Sections 3.4 and 4). What lies beyond the first store, if anything, is past an SOB. Nothing is the bound of the whole account, not an entry in it.

### 3.4 Accumulation and release

**Faces.** Storing, and letting go.

**Statement.** The dense objects at the centers of galaxies are not holes. They are galactic accumulators: stores that gather, hold and release, as a hydraulic accumulator holds pressure until it is needed. In plain words they are middens, the heaps where a galaxy’s leftovers collect and its history is layered. They are distinct from the remains of single collapsed stars, which we call collapsed stellar cores, or graves. A grave is a result, not a feature: what remains when a single star has finished its own gathering and release, the star’s burning and its final outburst. It is not a face of a pair but the residue of one, as entropy is the residue of scattering. A midden is a working store; it holds and returns. The largest release of all was the Big Bang, which we read as the release face of a galactic accumulator. Their garbage became our starting place.

**Record.** The central objects grow in step with their galaxies: the mass of the central object tracks the speed of the stars in the galaxy’s bulge, a relation found independently by two teams in 2000. Some were already enormous within the first few hundred million years: the object in UHZ1, seen about 470 million years after the Big Bang, is already tens of millions of solar masses. The centers switch on and off, flaring and fading over time. They blow cavities the size of galaxies in the hot gas around them, the record of repeated outbursts. Our own galaxy’s center has erupted: the Fermi bubbles, found in gamma rays in 2010, and the larger eROSITA bubbles, found in X-rays in 2020, rise tens of thousands of light-years above and below the galactic plane. Where it can be seen, inflow arrives through the disk and outflow leaves along the poles, the one direction where nothing is piled in the way.

**Consequence.** A hole only swallows. An accumulator charges and discharges, and the observations describe charging and discharging. The singularity, a point where the account breaks down, is a one-faced name for a place where the other face, release, has been left out. And if the largest accumulators release, the question of where the universe came from becomes a question of what released it. The release itself lies beyond an SOB: the earliest light we can see was set free about 380,000 years after the Big Bang, and nothing earlier reaches us directly.

### 3.5 Our universe and its sister

**Faces.** The result of the release, and its other half.

**Statement.** The release made a pair. Our universe is one face of the result; its sister is the other. Her matter is antimatter, her time runs the other way from the shared first moment, and her hand is the mirror of ours. She lies beyond an SOB, and touches us, if at all, only through what both halves share.

**Record.** Our universe is a lopsided ledger. It holds matter and almost no antimatter: about six baryons for every ten billion photons, the residue of a slight surplus in the early universe. No antimatter galaxies have been found, and the absence of annihilation radiation at any boundary between matter and antimatter regions rules out large antimatter domains within the observable universe. Our time runs one way. One of our forces, the weak force, distinguishes left from right, as Chien-Shiung Wu showed in 1957. In 1967 Andrei Sakharov set out the conditions under which a universe could make more matter than antimatter; physics has spent the decades since looking for a mechanism large enough, and has not found one.

**Consequence.** On the fourth principle, a lopsided ledger is not an accident. It is a map to the missing column. The binary view reads the matter surplus, the single arrow of time and the single preferred hand as three entries pointing to the same missing half. The question is not why the universe chose matter. It is where the antimatter went, and the answer the binary view gives is: to the other face of the result.

### 3.6 Gathering and dispersing

**Faces.** Motion advancing, and motion receding. Flood, and ebb.

**Statement.** Within our half, motion works in two directions in one medium. Motion advances and gathers matter; the outcome we call gravity. Motion recedes, and the debris that friction breaks off scatters; the outcome we call entropy. Gravity and entropy are names for outcomes. Motion is the player.

The image is a tidal bay. The tide flows in, the water goes slack at the changeover, and the tide flows out. One process, one medium, two directions. The tide flows until it meets resistance, and then it ebbs on the other side. Reality is a continuing tide as space expands: on the largest scale the expansion is the ebb, and wherever mass gathers the flood goes on.

Receding takes two forms. Locally, friction breaks ordered motion into debris and scatters it; on the largest scale, the medium itself spreads as space expands. We count them as one face because both carry matter apart. Whether they share a single mechanism is a question this paper leaves open.

**Record.** On gravity. A pressure difference in a fluid does not merely press; it makes the fluid flow. If the medium of space flows toward mass at the speed needed to escape from each distance, the acceleration of a body carried in it reproduces Newton’s law exactly. This is the content of a form of Einstein’s equations found by Painlevé in 1921 and Gullstrand in 1922, and developed as the “river model” by Hamilton and Lisle in 2008. The inflow explains why all bodies fall alike: they ride the same current. The MICROSCOPE satellite confirmed that universality to about one part in a thousand trillion in 2022. A falling body feels nothing; a body held still by the ground feels the current run past it. Weight is the push of a current we are not allowed to ride.

On entropy. Every increase of entropy has motion behind it, driven down a gradient and scattered by friction in one of its forms: the collisions of molecules, the viscosity of fluids, the resistance of conductors, the scattering of light. Where motion stops, entropy stops changing. Entropy measures the outcome; it does not act.

On the tide. The expansion of the universe stopped slowing and began to speed up five or six billion years ago. Star formation peaked about ten billion years ago. At present the gathering and the spreading are nearly in balance, a fact cosmology calls the coincidence problem. The binary view reads it as the tide near balance in its middle years.

**Consequence.** Gravity is not a force acting across empty space, and no particle is needed to carry it. Entropy is not a power steering the universe toward its end. The two are not opponents in a contest whose winner decides the fate of the universe; they are the outcomes of one activity going two ways. The arrow of time points the way motion is receding, and entropy is its record, not its cause. If the large-scale ebb is what this paper takes it to be, the acceleration of expansion belongs to it, and a separate dark energy is not required.

### 3.7 Constrained and free motion

**Faces.** Tension, and unused potential.

**Statement.** Energy is not a third member beside matter and motion. Physics defines energy as a conserved quantity, the capacity to do work, and leaves open what it is. In a material medium the question has an answer: energy is motion under constraint. Motion that is held back, by resistance, compression or confinement, becomes tension, and energy is that tension and its release. Motion that runs free carries its energy as unused potential: the tension it will become when it meets resistance, spent on whatever gets in its way. The conservation of energy is the ledger of the first pair.

**Record.** Potential energy is the medium compressed or strained. Mass is matter whose motion is confined in one place: Einstein’s 1905 relation between mass and energy says so from the other side, and the proton shows it. The rest masses of its three quarks add up to about one percent of its mass. Lattice calculations by the χQCD Collaboration in 2018 assign the rest to the energy of the quarks’ motion, the energy of the gluon field that binds them, and related terms. A proton weighs what it does because of the motion inside it with nowhere to go. Energy shows itself where motion meets resistance, at a friction point, as heat, light, a blow, a shock. And the energy of free motion is fixed only at the meeting: a body’s kinetic energy differs from one observer to the next and is settled only against the thing it strikes.

**Consequence.** Nobody was ever shocked by a bookkeeping system. Energy is physical because motion is physical. A shock is tension letting go; a star is confined motion leaking out as light; a mass is matter whose motion is held in place. The abstract number of the textbooks is the measure, and constrained motion is the thing measured.

### 3.8 Wave and particle

**Faces.** The medium moving, and the medium meeting resistance.

**Statement.** Space is a material medium. Light is its motion. What physics calls a particle is the medium meeting resistance, a disturbance localized where it is stopped. Wave and particle are one substance seen in two conditions: the pool and the drip. The pool is the medium spread and moving; the drip is the same medium gathered at a point where it is stopped. There is only water.

**Record.** Light travels as a wave and arrives as a particle; no experiment shows both faces at once, and none can do without either. Niels Bohr named the condition complementarity in 1927. Fluids reproduce some of the behavior of curved spacetime: in 1981 William Unruh showed that sound in a flowing fluid can have a horizon, the founding result of the field now called analog gravity.

**Consequence.** If space is a medium, the effects attributed to dark matter may be the medium’s own condition around mass rather than an unseen substance. The binary view adds only that wave and particle need no reconciling. They were never two things.

### 3.9 Twist and counter-twist

**Faces.** Matter and antimatter, positive and negative, north and south.

**Statement.** Every disturbance in the medium is made with its counter-disturbance. A pair is made in one act and unmade in one act.

**Record.** In 1928 Paul Dirac’s equation for the electron produced a second set of solutions describing nothing then known; in 1932 Carl Anderson found the positron in cosmic rays. In 1933 Patrick Blackett and Giuseppe Occhialini photographed high-energy light turning into an electron and a positron at one point. Every particle made in every accelerator arrives with its antiparticle. Electric charge has never been created or destroyed, only separated and rejoined. In 1918 Emmy Noether proved that every continuous symmetry of nature carries a conservation law.

**Consequence.** Nature does not issue a plus without its minus. The rule that governs the smallest pairs governs the largest one, the universe and its sister.

### 3.10 Action and reaction

**Faces.** Push, and push back.

**Statement.** No material face of a pair is ever found alone.

**Record.** In 1687 Newton stated that to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction; no push has been found without its push back. Cut a magnet and each piece has both poles. In 1931 Dirac showed that a lone magnetic pole would be consistent with quantum theory, and physicists have searched for one since in cosmic rays, in ancient rock and in accelerators; none has been found. No quark has been seen alone: pull two apart and the effort makes a new pair.

**Consequence.** Forces are pairs, not pulls. The search for a face without its partner, whatever the face, is a search the binary view expects to come back empty.

### 3.11 The rule through the coins

Running through every material coin is the same bookkeeping. Every entry has its counter-entry, and the whole of matter balances against the whole of motion. Merchants in Renaissance Italy are credited with inventing double-entry bookkeeping, and Luca Pacioli set it down in print in 1494. Nature had been using it all along.

Two working rules follow from it. **A lopsided ledger is a map to its missing face.** And **a name with one face names an outcome and hides a process.** The first found the positron and the neutrino. The second turns gravity, entropy and attraction back into motion.

## 4. From then to then

> Their garbage becomes our starting place.

Taken in sequence, the coins of Section 3 tell a story with a beginning and an end. The binary view asks only that the end, like every material entry, have its counter-entry.

### 4.1 Release

The story opens with a store letting go: the release face of a galactic accumulator, constrained motion becoming free. We call the event the Big Bang, and we see it only from the far side of an SOB, through the light set free some 380,000 years later.

### 4.2 Pair

On the second principle, energy becoming matter becomes a pair. The result of the release has another half: our universe and its sister.

### 4.3 Gathering and burning

Within our half the tide begins. Motion advances and gathers matter into stars and galaxies, and at their centers new accumulators begin to charge. Motion recedes, and the space between the gatherings grows. The stars burn their fuel, and in the light of the burning, matter in a few places arranges itself to know. The candle is lit by the bonfire. We live in the middle years, with the gathering and the spreading nearly in balance.

### 4.4 The end

The fuel runs out, because every store of it does; only nothing is inexhaustible. The stars go dark, and the debris of the universe collects in the last accumulators. The frame ends first: meaning lasts only while there are minds to make it, and the last knower goes out while the bonfire still smolders.

Physics tells the end as a heat death, an ending with no counter-entry. The binary view cannot accept a ledger with one column. The end is a storing, and a store is what our beginning came from. Their garbage became our starting place; ours may become someone else’s. The second principle also asks that our universe and its sister, made in one act, be unmade in one act. How and when that comes about, like the storing that feeds a later beginning, lies beyond an SOB.

## 5. The slope

> The observations are real. The smooth story isn’t.

### 5.1 What the two readings expect

The standard model of cosmology rests on the assumption that the universe, on large enough scales, is the same everywhere and in every direction. Our own motion through space produces a dipole, a hotter side and a cooler side, in the cosmic microwave background, and once that motion is removed, no direction is supposed to be special.

A tidal universe expects something different. A tide does not ebb evenly. A universe ebbing in a medium would be expected to show a preferred direction, a downhill. The two readings make different predictions about the same sky, and the sky has been measured.

### 5.2 Gradients by direction

Several independent groups, using different objects and different methods, have reported a preferred direction in the large-scale universe.

| Measurement | What was reported | Direction | Strength as reported
| Cosmic microwave background dipole (Planck) | Our motion of about 370 km/s relative to the background | Galactic l ≈ 264°, b ≈ 48°, toward Leo and Crater | Reference direction
| Matter dipole in quasars (Secrest et al. 2021) | About 1.4 million quasars counted across the sky; the dipole is about twice the size our motion predicts | Broadly aligned with the CMB dipole | 4.9σ; above 5σ in combination with radio galaxies (Secrest et al. 2025)
| Expansion rate by hemisphere (Luongo et al. 2022) | Larger values of the expansion rate in the hemisphere facing the CMB dipole, in quasars, strong-lensing time delays and supernovae | CMB dipole hemisphere | About 2 to 3σ
| Acceleration of expansion (Colin et al. 2019) | A dipole in the inferred acceleration from Type Ia supernovae | Aligned with the CMB dipole | Reported as significant; disputed by later analyses
| Large-scale bulk flows (summarized in Secrest et al. 2025) | Coherent motions of galaxies extending beyond the Shapley concentration | Broadly toward the same region | 3 to 5σ tension with the standard model
| Galaxy cluster scaling relations (Migkas et al. 2020, 2021) | An apparent 9 percent variation in the local expansion rate, or equivalently a bulk flow of about 900 km/s to at least 500 megaparsecs | Galactic l ≈ 280°, b ≈ −15° | Reported above 5σ in isotropic simulations
| Large-angle anomalies in the background radiation (Planck 2018) | A hemispherical difference in power, an unusually large cold spot, alignments among the largest-scale patterns | Various; some aligned with the dipole or the ecliptic | About 1 to 3σ each

Two features of the record stand out. The first is that most of the signals lean the same way, toward the broad region of sky marked by the dipole of the background radiation. The second is that the signals are not uniform in kind. The cluster result finds a lower expansion rate toward this region, where the quasar, lensing and supernova analyses find a higher one. The record agrees that the region is special; it does not yet agree on how. Separating a real anisotropy of the universe from an incomplete correction for our own motion is the central difficulty, and it is the work of the observers.

### 5.3 Gradients in time and distance

The expansion rate also differs with the epoch at which it is measured. Measured nearby, from Cepheid stars and supernovae, it comes out at about 73 kilometers per second per megaparsec (Riess et al. 2022). Inferred from the early universe through the background radiation, it comes out at about 67.4 (Planck 2018). The gap has grown more significant as the measurements have improved, and is known as the Hubble tension. In 2024 and 2025 the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument reported that the push attributed to dark energy appears to weaken with time, at significances between about 2.8 and 4.2σ depending on the supernova sample combined with it. And some astronomers argue that the Milky Way sits within a large region of low density, which would make local expansion appear faster.

### 5.4 Reading the record

The standard model treats each of these results as a separate puzzle, to be resolved one at a time by better corrections, larger samples or new physics added to the model. The binary, tidal reading treats them as one fact seen several ways: the universe is not ebbing evenly. It has a slope in direction and a slope in time.

We do not claim that the record proves the reading. Several of the signals are modest, they do not all point the same way, and some have been disputed. We claim that a preferred direction is what a tidal universe would produce, that it is not what a universe assumed to be the same in every direction would produce, and that most of the evidence for a gradient does not scatter randomly across the sky. It leans.

## 6. What changes

> We know what we sense. We assume what it is.

Nothing in the cosmos changes if the binary view is adopted. The cosmos has kept its books by double entry without our help. What changes is in the frame: the questions asked, the objects sought, and the story told.

### 6.1 For physics

**The goal of unification.** Physics has sought for a century a single force, a single field, a theory of everything that begins with one. The binary view holds that the bottom is two. The goal becomes one pair, matter and motion, with everything else an arrangement of it.

**The search for carriers.** Gravity is treated as a thing needing a particle to carry it, and the particle has not been found. No one searches for a particle of entropy, because entropy is accepted as an outcome. Granted the same standing, gravity needs no carrier, and the question moves to the motion of the medium.

**Action at a distance.** Forces between separated bodies, whether gravity or the attraction of opposite charges, become the medium’s own motion or the tendency of one disturbance to be whole. A pull across empty space disappears from the account, and space must be a medium for the account to work.

**Gravity and the second law.** The two are taught as separate subjects, one belonging to relativity, the other to thermodynamics. As outcomes of motion advancing and receding, they become one subject: motion in a medium, with two outcomes to account for. The popular contest between gravity building and entropy destroying disappears; outcomes do not compete.

**The arrow of time.** Physics explains time’s direction by the rise of entropy, which makes an outcome the cause of its own process. On the binary view the arrow points the way motion recedes, and entropy is its record.

**Black holes and singularities.** A region that only swallows is a ledger with one column. At the centers of galaxies, accumulators that charge and discharge replace holes; the remains of single stars are graves, residues rather than drains; and singularities are read as places where the release face has been left out of the account.

**Dark matter and dark energy.** These are entries added to balance books that do not otherwise balance. A physics that expects every entry to have its counter-entry looks first at what the existing pair is doing on the side we do not see, before adding an ingredient.

**Imbalances.** The surplus of matter, the single arrow of time and the single preferred hand are treated as accidents requiring fine-tuned explanations. The binary view treats them as maps to the missing face.

**Energy.** Energy acquires a body. It is constrained motion, and its conservation is the ledger of the first pair.

**The large-scale universe.** A universe assumed to be the same in every direction becomes a universe expected to have a slope, and the reports of a preferred direction become evidence rather than anomalies.

**The end.** Heat death, an ending with no counter-entry, becomes a storing, and a store is what a beginning comes from.

**Method.** “Find the other face” stops being a fortunate reasoning that worked twice, for the positron and the neutrino, and becomes the standing rule.

### 6.2 For knowledge

Every piece of knowledge acquires its other face: what is known, and the SOB beyond which our methods run out though something surely lies beyond. An honest account draws both. A map with no edge is not a more complete map; it is a map that has forgotten where it stops.

The question “what is this?” is joined by “what is this the other face of?”, and the second question works on every rung, from the quark to the end of the universe. Names that show one face, of which physics has several, are no longer mistaken for explanations.

### 6.3 For the knower

The old division of mind and matter gives way to one Reality and one frame: matter and motion in the cosmos, mind and meaning in the knower who frames it. In the knower’s own pairings, which are cognitive and not material, death is not an intrusion from outside but life’s other face, present from the beginning, and every decision carries the knower’s principal duality, to be or not to be, caution or curiosity, this or nothing. Insignificance and uniqueness cease to be a contradiction; they are the two faces of the knower, minute in the cosmos and the only place the cosmos is known.

And the knower knows something the bonfire does not: that the story has an end, and that even the end has its counter-entry.

## 7. Supporting witnesses

> Intelligence should always be respected, no matter what form it comes in.

The account is ours. Several witnesses stood near parts of it, and we call them in turn.

**Heraclitus**, around 500 BC, wrote that the road up and the road down are one and the same, and that people fail to see how a thing at variance with itself agrees with itself, like the opposing tension of the bow and the lyre. He saw opposites as one process seen from two sides. He did not name the first pair.

**Niels Bohr**, in 1927, proposed that light and matter show two faces, wave and particle, that cannot be seen at once and are both required for a complete account. When Denmark awarded him its highest honor in 1947, he chose for his coat of arms the yin-yang symbol and the motto _Contraria sunt complementa_: opposites are complementary. He applied the idea to the quantum and, in later lectures, beyond it. He did not trace a ladder of pairs.

**Paul Painlevé** in 1921 and **Allvar Gullstrand** in 1922 found a form of Einstein’s equations in which space flows inward toward mass. **Andrew Hamilton and Jason Lisle** in 2008 developed it as the river model, in which space falls into a black hole like a river over a waterfall. They treated the flow as a mathematical description. We read it as the current of Section 3.6.

**Andrei Sakharov**, in 1967, set out the conditions under which a universe could make more matter than antimatter, giving the lopsided ledger its formal statement. In 1980 he also considered cosmological models in which the arrow of time reverses on the other side of the initial moment.

**Latham Boyle, Kieran Finn and Neil Turok**, in 2018, proposed that the universe after the Big Bang is the mirror image, in charge, parity and time together, of a universe before it: a universe and an anti-universe forming one pair that emerges from nothing, with the arrow of time pointing away from the bang in both directions. Theirs is the nearest witness to Section 3.5. They reached the pair through the symmetries of quantum field theory; we reached it through the principle that a lopsided ledger points to its other face.

**Richard Tolman**, in 1934, examined universes that expand and contract in cycles, and **Roger Penrose**, in 2010, proposed a conformal cyclic cosmology in which the remote future of one age of the universe becomes the beginning of the next. Each stood near Section 4. Neither placed the beginning and the end within a theory of pairs.

What none of the witnesses did was name the first pair, set the pairs in order, or read the whole of physics as double-entry bookkeeping. That is the claim of this paper.

## 8. Objections and replies

> Always is not a word in science.

**Objection 1: this is a way of talking, not a theory.**

_Reply._ It is a way of seeing, and it stands on the record. Its third principle says no material face of a pair is found alone, and none has been. Its fourth says a lopsided ledger points to a missing face; that reasoning found the positron and the neutrino. And its tidal account of expansion expects a slope in the sky, which several independent measurements report (Section 5).

**Objection 2: nature also makes threes.** Quarks come in three colors, and protons are made of three quarks.

_Reply._ Each color has its anticolor, and the three combine into a whole that carries no color at all. The bookkeeping is still paired: every charge with its opposite, every color with its anticolor.

**Objection 3: energy has an exact definition, and calling it motion loses precision.**

_Reply._ The definition is kept as the measure. The binary view says what the measure is a measure of: motion under constraint, held as tension or carried as unused potential. Nothing in the arithmetic of energy changes. The frame dependence of kinetic energy, fixed only against what a moving body strikes, fits the account rather than troubling it.

**Objection 4: the Big Bang was not an explosion in space, so it cannot have been the release of an object.**

_Reply._ The standard account of the beginning also stops at an SOB; the earliest light we see was released about 380,000 years after the event, and what came before is inferred. The binary view does not claim to see past that boundary. It claims that a beginning, like every other entry, has a counter-entry, and that the counter-entry is a store. Which picture of the earliest moment is closer to Reality is a question beyond the boundary for both.

**Objection 5: a sister universe beyond observation cannot be checked.**

_Reply._ The sister lies beyond an SOB, and the paper says so. What lies on our side of the boundary is the lopsided ledger itself: the surplus of matter, the single arrow of time, the single preferred hand. Those are observed, and the sister is the reading the fourth principle gives them. Boyle, Finn and Turok have shown that a universe paired with an anti-universe is consistent with the known symmetries of physics.

**Objection 6: the reports of a preferred direction may be errors in correcting for our own motion, or other systematic effects.**

_Reply._ Some of them may be. The signals are of uneven strength, one runs opposite to the others, and several have been disputed. What the binary view notes is that most of them lean the same way, that they come from different objects and different methods, and that a tidal universe expects a lean. Sorting the real from the artificial belongs to the observers.

**Objection 7: an end that stores what a later beginning releases implies a purpose, a universe arranged to feed its successor.**

_Reply._ It implies none. Gathering is what motion does in a medium when there is no fuel left to burn. A store that is later released is ordinary motion at an extraordinary scale.

**Objection 8: if gravity is an inflow, the inflowing medium must go somewhere.**

_Reply._ It does, and the answer is the tidal bay: the inflow carries matter to a friction point, the pile grows until its resistance balances the flow, and the flow reroutes and returns, as the outflows along the poles of galactic centers return what the disks deliver. On the largest scale, the ebb is the expansion.

**Objection 9: matter at absolute zero would not move, so the first pair can be separated.**

_Reply._ Absolute zero cannot be reached, and quantum physics holds that matter retains a residual motion even in its lowest state. Matter without motion is a limit, never a thing.

**Objection 10: Bohr’s complementarity holds that wave and particle are two descriptions that can never be merged into one picture.**

_Reply._ The binary view does not merge them. It agrees that the two faces cannot be seen at once; that is what it means to be the faces of a coin. Heads and tails are never seen together, and no one concludes that there are two coins. Complementarity describes the coin from the side of the observer. The binary view adds the coin: wave and particle, pool and drip, are the two faces of one medium.

**Objection 11: the proposal has no mathematics, and a proposal in physics becomes physics only when it can be calculated.**

_Reply._ A thing has to be described before an equation can be set on top of it. Michael Faraday, who had little mathematical training, described the electric and magnetic field as lines of force filling space, and was doubted for it. James Clerk Maxwell, beginning with his 1855 paper On Faraday’s Lines of Force, put equations on Faraday’s description, and the result became the foundation of electromagnetism. This paper is a description. The equations, if it earns them, belong to those equipped to write them.

**Objection 12: a material medium of space is the luminiferous ether revived, and the ether failed.**

_Reply._ The ether was proposed because the mathematics of waves seemed to require something to wave. It was an entry added to make an equation balance, the dark matter of its day, and when the experiments of Michelson and Morley in 1887 found no trace of the stationary frame it implied, it was set aside. The medium of this paper is not proposed to rescue an equation. It follows from the premise that Reality is material and from the first pair: there is no motion without something moving, and light travels. The ether was required by mathematics; the medium is required by the structure of Reality as the binary view reads it.

## 9. Conclusion

> Matter and motion. Mind and meaning.

Reality is material, and its first pair is matter and motion: what is there, and what it does. The knower frames it, and the frame has its own working pair, mind and meaning, seeing one face at a time. Every material pair in nature is one thing with two faces, made together and unmade together, never found with one face alone. A lopsided pair points to its missing face, and a name that shows one face names an outcome and hides a process. Reality keeps its accounts by double entry.

Read in that light, the universe tells one story. A galactic accumulator releases. The release becomes a pair, our universe and its sister. Within our half, motion advances and gathers, and recedes and scatters its debris; we name the outcomes gravity and entropy. Energy is motion under constraint, held as tension and released where motion meets resistance. In the middle years, while the fuel burns, matter in a few places arranges itself to know, and the candle is lit by the bonfire. The fuel runs out, and the debris gathers in the last accumulators. The end is a storing, and a store is what a beginning comes from. The record of the sky shows a preferred direction of the kind such a tide would leave.

What seems clearly not right is a physics that treats the pairs of nature as coincidences, its imbalances as accidents, its names for outcomes as causes, and its end as a ledger with one column.

The better question is not what the universe is made of. It is what each thing in it is the other face of, and where that other face has gone.

_We are storytellers, not scientists. These are ideas, not facts. If they are facts, we cannot prove it._

## Abstract

Belief in luck and fate is among the most widespread and durable beliefs people hold. It appears in every culture and century, among the educated and the uneducated alike, and it survives every argument made against it. Expert opinion treats it as error: a cluster of cognitive biases, superstition, magical thinking. That diagnosis explains the distortions in the belief, but not the belief itself, and it carries a quiet condescension toward the people who hold it.

We propose a different reading, in the terms of the binary view of Reality. **Fate is the supplier:** the unseen web of causes, too large and too fine for anyone to trace, that delivers whatever arrives in a life. **The luck twins are the faces:** good luck and bad luck, the two ways a delivery lands on the one who receives it. The supplier is material. The twins are the knower’s names for what it delivers. On this reading the folk are not wrong that something beyond their sight shapes their lives. They are right about that, and wrong only about what it is, which is the same kind of mistake physics makes when it turns a name into a thing.

## 1. A belief that will not go away

> Everyone makes mistakes. Some of us just make more.

Most people privately believe that luck and fate are real. They knock on wood after good news, speak of a lucky break and a run of bad luck, and say of a turn in their lives that it was meant to be. In 2005 a Gallup poll found that about three Americans in four held at least one belief of this general kind. Scientists knock on wood too.

The standard account treats all of it as malfunction. The gambler’s fallacy, the illusion of control, the human appetite for patterns in noise: each is real, each is well documented, and together they explain why people misjudge chance. But a belief that appears everywhere, in every age, and outlives every refutation is a fact in its own right. An explanation that calls it an error has explained the error, not the persistence.

This paper asks what the persistent belief is tracking.

## 2. The supplier

A stochastic process is one whose outcomes cannot be predicted in detail, only described in their spread. The word does not require that nothing causes the outcomes. It says that the causes are too many, too small or too tangled to follow. A die is governed by ordinary physics, yet the throw depends on so many fine conditions that its face cannot be foretold. In 1963 the meteorologist Edward Lorenz showed that weather has the same character: changes too small to measure grow until they decide whether it rains.

Every human life sits inside such a web. A letter arrives on the day it does because of a postal route, a sorting machine, a driver’s breakfast. A career turns on who happened to read an application. A life is spared because a truck left two minutes late. No one can trace these chains, and no one could, because they branch without end.

This web is what we mean by **fate**. Not a script written in advance, and not a personality with intentions, but the supplier: the whole unseen traffic of causes that delivers what arrives. It is material, made of matter and motion like everything else. And it lies, for each of us, beyond an SOB, a scientific observational boundary: the place where our ability to trace causes runs out, though something surely lies beyond.

## 3. The luck twins

What the supplier delivers lands on the knower in one of two ways. A delivery better than expected we call **good luck**. A delivery worse than expected we call **bad luck**. These are the luck twins, and they are the two faces of one supply.

The twins are conjoined. Any opening to the world that admits a windfall admits a blow by the same door. The venture that might succeed might fail; the road that leads to the chance meeting leads to the accident. A life sealed off from bad luck would be sealed off from good luck as well. The deliveries that earn both names come by the same exposure.

They also echo the balance the binary view finds in material pairs, though here the balance is arithmetic rather than physical. Measured against the true average of what the supplier delivers, every delivery falls above or below it, and those deviations sum toward zero by the definition of an average. The knower’s own expectation carries no such guarantee, which is part of why luck feels lopsided (Section 4).

The twins are cognitive constructions. The binary principles govern material features, and the supplier is material; good and bad are the knower’s judgments about what it supplies. Nothing in the web of causes is good or bad. A frost is good luck for the ski resort and bad luck for the orchard on the same morning.

## 4. Why the twins are hard to see

If the twins balance, why do people experience luck as streaky, personal and often unkind? The record offers three reasons, each consistent with the reading above.

**We see one face at a time.** A delivery lands as one twin or the other, never both. The knower meets a run of good luck, then a run of bad, and never sees them as faces of one supply.

**We weigh the faces unequally.** In 2001 the psychologist Roy Baumeister and colleagues reviewed a large body of research under the title “Bad Is Stronger Than Good.” Losses, insults and misfortunes weigh more heavily and last longer in memory than gains of the same size. The deliveries may balance on average; the knower’s ledger of them tilts.

**The faces are not always the same size.** The balance holds only on average and in the long run. A life is a short run, many small good breaks may never arrive in time to offset one catastrophe, and a single delivery can be large enough to change everything after it. This is why people insure against the bad twin and do not insure against the good one.

Two further findings show how much of an outcome the supplier decides. In 2018 three physicists, Alessandro Pluchino, Alessio Biondo and Andrea Rapisarda, simulated many careers, giving each person some talent and a lifetime of random breaks. The most successful were rarely the most talented; they were people of middling talent who received the most good breaks. And the psychologist Richard Wiseman, who spent years studying people who described themselves as lucky or unlucky, found that much of the difference lay in what they noticed: the self-described lucky were more likely to see an opportunity that the supplier had put in front of everyone.

The last finding shows the knower’s part. The supplier delivers to all; the knower decides what to pick up. Daniel Kahneman described flight instructors who believed that praise made pilots worse and criticism made them better, when the change was only the next delivery returning toward the average. The instructors saw the twins and missed the supplier.

## 5. What the folk see, and what the experts miss

The folk see something real. They perceive that their lives are shaped by forces beyond their sight, which is true. They give the supplier a name, fate, and give its two ways of landing names, good and bad luck. Their error is to take the names for agents: fate as a will, luck as a property a person can carry, as if the supplier had favorites.

The experts see the folk’s error and stop there. Having shown that the belief distorts chance, they conclude that nothing is being perceived. That is the larger mistake. The web of causes is not imaginary; it is most of what happens. Calling the perception of it a bias is like calling the perception of weather a bias because people misjudge the odds of rain.

The pattern is familiar from physics. Gravity is the name for an outcome, matter gathered, and was mistaken for a force. Luck is a name for outcomes too, and fate, taken for an agent, hides the very process it names. The cure is the same: keep the names, and restore the process behind them.

And the folk practices make more sense on this reading than on the expert one. Knocking on wood after good news is an acknowledgment that the good twin arrived from a supplier that also ships the bad. It is a recognition of the pair, not a belief that wood has powers.

## 6. Objections and replies

**Objection 1: luck is nothing but statistical variance.**

_Reply._ Variance is the measure; the supplier is the thing measured. A number describing the spread of outcomes does not deliver them. The paper keeps the statistics and asks what they are statistics of.

**Objection 2: “fate” implies that everything is determined in advance.**

_Reply._ Not as the word is used here. The supplier is a web of causes, not a script. Whether every strand in it is fixed, or some are genuinely open, lies past an SOB; the reading needs only that the strands are too many to trace.

**Objection 3: dignifying luck and fate encourages superstition.**

_Reply._ It does the opposite. It takes the perception seriously and corrects the error inside it. A person who sees fate as a supplier rather than a will has no reason to bargain with it, and every reason to notice what it delivers.

**Objection 4: if the twins balance, there is nothing to explain.**

_Reply._ They balance in the long run and in expectation. A life is a short run, the faces can differ greatly in size, and the knower weighs them unequally. What needs explaining is the experience, and the experience is what the twins describe.

## 7. Conclusion

The belief in luck and fate is universal because the thing it perceives is universal: a web of causes, larger than any life, delivering what arrives. Fate is the supplier. Good luck and bad luck are the twin names the knower gives its deliveries, conjoined because the same exposure brings both kinds, and seen one at a time. The supplier is material; the twins are the knower’s names for its deliveries.

What seems clearly not right is a science that explains away a universal human perception as a malfunction, and a folk belief that mistakes the supplier for a personality.

The better question is not why people believe in luck. It is what they are perceiving when they do.

## References

- Baumeister, R. F., Bratslavsky, E., Finkenauer, C. and Vohs, K. D. (2001). Bad is stronger than good. _Review of General Psychology_ 5, 323.
- Kahneman, D. (2011). _Thinking, Fast and Slow_. New York: Farrar, Straus and Giroux.

## Abstract

_The Candle and the Bonfire_ proposed a binary view of Reality: Reality is material, its first pair is matter and motion, and every material pair in nature is one thing with two faces. It counted the medium of space as matter and described a particle as that medium gathered and held where its motion is confined. It left one question open: where space itself sits in the binary.

We propose an answer. **Space and matter are one medium at different densities.** Matter is space gathered; space is matter spread thin. Dense and rare are the two faces, and density is the dial between them. One straight line shows the whole dial. Run it from the center of a galactic accumulator, the densest place we can infer, out through its event horizon and into the thin space between galaxies, and it crosses the dial from its densest reach to its rarest. The same line runs through time: it begins with a release that established our space and ends with the storing that may establish someone else’s. That line is the spine of this paper. Density is not a third member beside matter and motion. It is the measure of their partnership: how much matter is gathered in a place, and how its motion is held there. Motion turns the dial. Confined motion concentrates; freed motion spreads.

Read this way, the coins of the binary view become movements on a single dial. Gathering and dispersing, the outcomes named gravity and entropy, are the dial turning up and turning down. Accumulation and release, the Big Bang and the storing at the end, are the same dial on the largest scale. A particle is a knot of density in the medium, with a duration rather than a destiny.

The dial also has two ends, and neither is a place where anything real can sit. Infinite density is the singularity that physics already treats as a breakdown. Zero density is nothing, which the binary view already treats as the bound of the whole account. Everything real lives in between. This gives a principled reason to reject infinite density, and it applies with equal force to the other infinities physics is content to keep: particles that never decay and space that never ends.

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1 The open question

A binary view of Reality has to say where space belongs. If space were empty, a stage on which matter performs, it would be a second kind of thing, and the premise that Reality is material would fail at the first step. If space were matter’s partner, a face opposite to matter, the first pair would be matter and space, not matter and motion. Neither fits.

_The Candle and the Bonfire_ avoided both by counting the medium of space as matter. That was a definition. This paper offers the relation behind it.

### 1.2 The proposal in one line

> Matter is space gathered. Space is matter spread thin.

### 1.3 Where this paper stands

This is a companion to _The Candle and the Bonfire_, and it uses that paper’s premise, terms and five principles without restating their full support. Like its companion, it is an argument from the record, not a mathematical theory. It proposes a way of seeing and checks it against what has been observed.

## 2. The proposal

### 2.1 One medium, two faces

**Faces.** Dense and rare.

**Statement.** Space and matter are one material medium at different densities. Where the medium is gathered and held, we call it matter; where it is spread thin, we call it space. The difference between them is a difference of degree, not of kind. Dense and rare are faces of one coin in the sense of the binary view: neither is found without the other, and every gathering in one place is a thinning somewhere else.

### 2.2 Density is a measure, not a player

Density is not a substance and does nothing by itself. It is the measure of how the first pair is arranged in a place: how much matter is there, and how its motion is held. On the fifth principle, a name with one face names an outcome and hides a process. Density, read alone, would be such a name. Read with its other face, rarity, it is the dial on which the first pair shows its condition.

### 2.3 Motion turns the dial

Motion is the player, as in _The Candle and the Bonfire_. Motion held in place, confined by resistance, compression or its own turning back, gathers the medium and raises its density. Motion set free carries the medium apart and lowers it. Every movement on the dial is motion doing one of these two things.

### 2.4 The spine: one line through an accumulator

Draw a straight line from the center of a galactic accumulator outward.

It begins where the medium is gathered more densely than anywhere else we can infer. The center lies behind the horizon, beyond an SOB, a scientific observational boundary, where our methods of observation run out though something surely lies beyond. We infer its density; we do not see it. Physics calls this place a singularity. The binary view refines it into an accumulator: the same densest place, with finite density and with its other face, release, restored.

Moving outward, the density falls. The line crosses the event horizon. In the river form of Einstein’s equations, the horizon is where the medium flowing inward reaches the speed of light: inside, everything is carried in; outside, light can still climb out. The horizon is not a wall. It is a mark on the dial, the place where gathering outruns escape.

Beyond the horizon the line runs through the galaxy’s gathered stars and gas, where density rises and falls with every star it passes, and then out into the space between galaxies, the rarest the record shows.

One line, dense to rare. Every material coin of the binary view lies somewhere along it, and the sections below read each coin as a segment of this line.

### 2.5 The spine in time: release establishes space

The line is not only a map. It is a history. Density is not just a reading on a dial; it is what a release does. When an accumulator lets go, it ejects the medium it held, and the medium, spread thin, is space. Space is not a container in which the release happened. The release established it.

On this reading our space began when another accumulator released, the Big Bang of _The Candle and the Bonfire_: their garbage became our starting place. And our line ends when the debris of our universe has gathered in the last accumulators, ready for a release that may establish someone else’s. The line runs from their release to our storing, then to then. Its spatial form, from a dense center out to the rare space beyond, is the same history read at one moment.

## 3. The coins on one dial

The binary view orders its material coins from the most fundamental down. Each, we suggest, is the density dial seen at a particular scale.

### 3.1 Matter and motion

The first pair remains the first pair. Density adds no member to it. It names the result of the partnership in any one place: the medium as much gathered as its motion holds it.

### 3.2 Gathering and dispersing

_The Candle and the Bonfire_ described motion advancing and gathering matter, the outcome named gravity, and motion receding and scattering its debris, the outcome named entropy. On the dial, gathering is density rising and dispersing is density falling. Gravity and entropy are names for the dial turning one way and the other. The tide of that paper, flood and ebb in one medium, is the dial moving through a bay.

### 3.3 Accumulation and release

An accumulator is a place where the dial is turned up and held. A release lets it fall. The Big Bang, read as the release face of a galactic accumulator, is the largest fall the record allows us to infer. The end, read as a storing, is the dial being turned up again in the last accumulators. Their garbage became our starting place, and on the dial that means density gathered in one era becomes the source of the next.

### 3.4 Constrained and free motion

Energy, on the binary view, is motion under constraint: motion held back becomes tension, and energy is that tension and its release. A medium under constraint is a medium compressed. Potential energy is the dial held higher than the motion in that place would leave it. Release lets it fall back, and the motion runs free.

### 3.5 Wave and particle

The pool and the drip are the medium spread and the medium gathered at a point. The wave is the dial low and moving; the particle is the dial high where the motion is stopped. There is only water, at two densities.

### 3.6 Particles: durations, not destinies

A particle is a knot of density, the medium gathered and held where its motion is confined. A knot lasts as long as its confinement lasts. Nothing in the medium holds a knot permanently, and nothing in the binary view requires that any knot be permanent. A particle has a duration, however long, not a destiny.

### 3.7 The rule through the dial

Every material coin, read this way, is the one medium gathering and spreading under the play of its own motion. The double entry of nature appears on the dial as a rule: every gathering here is a thinning elsewhere, and the books of density balance across the whole.

## 4. The two limits

### 4.1 Both ends of the dial

A dial has ends. At one end is infinite density, all of the medium gathered into no room at all. At the other is zero density, no medium at all. We propose that both ends are limits, not states. Nothing real has been found at either, and the binary view gives a reason why nothing real can be.

### 4.2 Infinite density

General relativity, carried to its conclusion, predicts points of infinite density at the beginning of the universe and at the centers of collapsed objects. The singularity theorems of Penrose and Hawking showed that, under broad conditions, the theory leads there. Physicists nearly all read this as the place where the theory stops describing nature, not as a description of something that exists.

The binary view agrees and supplies the reason. Every gathering is matched by a thinning elsewhere. The counter-entry to an infinite gathering would be an infinite thinning, which is nothing, and nothing is the bound of the account, not an entry in it. A point of infinite density would be a face whose other face is nothing: a face alone. On the third principle, no face is found alone. The accumulator is the refinement of the singularity: the densest point on the spine, with finite density and a release. _The Candle and the Bonfire_ reads the dense objects at the centers of galaxies this way, as stores that hold and release, not as holes ending in a point.

### 4.3 Zero density

At the other end lies nothing. _The Candle and the Bonfire_ treats nothing as the bound of the whole account: not a substance, not a partner, the limit against which everything found is something. Zero density is that bound seen on the dial. Physics agrees in its own way: the vacuum it measures is never empty.

### 4.4 Everything real lives in between

If both ends of the dial are limits, every real thing has a density that is more than nothing and less than infinite. The spine shows it: the line begins at the densest place, not at infinity, and ends in the rarest, not in nothing. The most rarefied regions of space still hold the medium; the densest objects still have room.

### 4.5 The convenient infinity

Physics treats its infinities unevenly. Infinite density is rejected as a breakdown. Infinite space, for a flat universe of the simplest shape, is widely entertained. Infinite time, for particles that have never been seen to decay, is accepted, and the far future of the universe is told as a thin haze of such particles drifting apart forever.

The density dial treats them alike. A particle that lasts forever would be a knot that never loosens in a medium that never stops moving, a permanent state in a medium where every other state passes. The experiments themselves claim less. They report that a proton, if it decays, lasts more than about 10^34 years: a floor, not a finding. And the companion paper _The Whole Car_ argues that straight light across the visible universe says nothing about the shape of the whole, which may be bounded. On the binary view, infinity in any direction lies beyond an SOB. The principle that rules out infinite density rules out the others as well. What seems clearly not right is accepting the infinities that comfort a theory while rejecting the one that embarrasses it.

## 5. The record

**The vacuum is not empty.** Quantum theory assigns empty space a residual zero-point motion in every mode. In 1948 Hendrik Casimir predicted that two uncharged metal plates placed close together in a vacuum would be pushed toward each other, and Steve Lamoreaux measured the effect in 1997. On the usual reading, empty space has a measurable condition. The speed of light, the permittivity and permeability of free space and the expansion of the universe are further properties of something, not of nothing. Einstein reached a related conclusion late in life: “There is no such thing as an empty space, i.e. a space without field. Space-time does not claim existence on its own, but only as a structural quality of the field.”

**Density is the variable cosmology already runs on.** Since Friedmann’s equations of 1922, the large-scale behavior of the universe has been calculated from its density compared with a critical density, today equivalent to a few hydrogen atoms per cubic meter. The binary view does not add density to cosmology. It reads it as the coin itself rather than a parameter.

**The range is enormous and finite.** The thin gas between the stars holds around one atom per cubic centimeter, and the space between galaxies far less. Ordinary matter runs from air to lead. A neutron star packs more than a solar mass into a sphere the size of a city, near the density of an atomic nucleus. Nothing observed directly is denser. Even the largest dark central objects are not dense on average: measured by the radius of their horizons, the average density of an object of a hundred million suns is comparable to water, and that of the largest is thinner than air. No measured density is infinite, and no measured region is empty.

**Mass is confined motion.** The rest masses of a proton’s three quarks add up to about one percent of its mass. Lattice calculations assign most of the rest to the motion of the quarks and the energy of the field that binds them. A proton weighs what it does because of the motion held inside it: a knot of density, held by confinement.

**No knot is found alone.** No quark has been seen by itself. Pulling two apart takes so much energy that a new pair is made, and the result is two bound sets, not a free quark. The densest knots in nature come in pairs and triples.

## 6. What changes

**For physics.** The singularity becomes a limit the medium approaches and never reaches; the central objects of galaxies become stores with finite density and a release. The heat death becomes a thinning that is followed by a gathering, not a haze that lasts forever. Particles become conditions with durations. The vacuum becomes the medium at its rare end, not a stage. And density, already central to cosmology, becomes the coin rather than one parameter among many.

**For the binary view.** The open question of space is closed. Space is not a stage and not a partner: it is the rare face of the one medium. Every material coin becomes a movement on one dial, and the theme that runs through all of them is gathering and spreading, played by motion, with nothing real at either end.

## 7. Objections and replies

**Objection 1. Density is a quantity, not a thing. A dial cannot be a coin.**

_Reply._ Agreed that density is a measure. The claim is not that density acts. Motion acts. The claim is that space and matter differ in degree, not in kind, and that dense and rare are the two faces of that one difference. Temperature is a measure too, and hot and cold are still a pair.

**Objection 2. Space is not made of anything. Its density is zero by definition.**

_Reply._ Space that is defined as empty cannot be measured, and space as measured is not empty. It has zero-point motion, it pushes plates together, it carries light at a fixed speed, and it expands. On the binary view, a thing with measurable properties is something. Its density is very low, not zero.

**Objection 3. This revives the ether, which Michelson and Morley disproved in 1887.**

_Reply._ Michelson and Morley found no wind of a fixed ether against the moving Earth. The medium of _The Candle and the Bonfire_ is not fixed; it flows with mass, as in the river form of Einstein’s equations, and a medium moving with the bodies in it produces no such wind. The ether was a placeholder parked in a gap to carry light. The medium here is the material of space, read from what space is measured to do.

**Objection 4. General relativity predicts infinite density. Rejecting it rejects the theory.**

_Reply._ Physicists themselves read the infinity as the place where the theory stops, and spend careers looking for what takes over. We accept the theory where it is measured and decline its conclusion where it is agreed to fail.

**Objection 5. An electron is not simply dense space. Density cannot tell an electron from a proton.**

_Reply._ Agreed. Density locates a particle; it does not specify it. The binary view distinguishes particles by their motion as well, and by twist and counter-twist, as _The Candle and the Bonfire_ sets out. The dial says where the medium is gathered, not every way in which it is held.

**Objection 6. If no particle lasts forever, when does an electron decay?**

_Reply._ We do not know, and we make no prediction. The claim is narrower: “never seen to decay” is not “never decays,” and nothing in the binary view requires any condition of a moving medium to be permanent. The question lies beyond an SOB.

## 8. Conclusion

> Matter is space gathered. Space is matter spread thin.

The binary view began with a premise, that Reality is material, and a first pair, matter and motion. It left open where space belongs. Space belongs on the dial, and it was put there by a release. One straight line shows it: from the center of an accumulator, through its event horizon, out into the space between galaxies. One medium, gathered and spread by its own motion, appears as matter where it is dense and as space where it is rare. Gravity and entropy name the dial turning; accumulators hold it high and release lets it fall; particles are knots on it with durations, not destinies. Both ends of the dial are limits. Infinite density and true emptiness are where description stops, and everything real lives in between.

What seems clearly not right is a physics that rejects infinite density as a breakdown while accepting infinite lives for particles and entertaining infinite extent for space.

The better question is not whether space is empty or full. It is how densely the one medium is gathered in each place, what motion holds it there, and where the other face of each gathering has gone.
